title: UEFA, Concacaf, AFC accuse FIFA of 'breach of trust,' 'deception' over World Cup plan
dek: Three continental confederations have formally accused FIFA President Gianni Infantino of systematic deception over plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors. The confederations say the compressed timeline and lack of consultation violated fundamental trust. They are calling for an independent review and have held preliminary discussions about organizing their own tournaments.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: UEFA, Concacaf, and AFC issued a joint statement accusing FIFA of a 'fundamental breach of trust' and 'deception' over the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell approximately 20% to private investors.
bottom_line: The formal accusation from three confederations representing Europe, North America, Central America, and the Caribbean and Asia represents a rare moment of unified opposition to FIFA's leadership. What to watch: whether Infantino resigns before March, what shape an independent review takes if granted, and whether preliminary confederation discussions about independent tournaments move beyond talks to concrete structure.
body: UEFA, Concacaf, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) have formally accused FIFA of a 'fundamental breach of trust' and 'deception' over its handling of plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors, according to ESPN's reporting. The accusation marks an unprecedented escalation in the public conflict between the continental confederations and FIFA President Gianni Infantino.

The three confederations took aim directly at Infantino, saying the process represented a 'profound failure of judgment' and accusing him of acting like someone who 'believes the game is answerable to him,' per the same reporting. The target of their criticism was Infantino's proposal to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a company designed to run the commercial and operational aspects of FIFA's tournaments, with a plan to sell around 20% to private investors.

In a joint statement quoted by ESPN, the confederations alleged deliberate obfuscation: 'A proposal advanced on a compressed timeline, without meaningful consultation, and pushed toward a deadline before member associations could properly review its terms is not the product of an oversight, it is the product of a design intended to limit scrutiny.' They characterized the attempt to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup as 'a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve.'

Infantino apologized for the FFE proposal, according to ESPN. However, the confederations have not treated the apology as sufficient. Instead, they have urged FIFA to conduct an independent review into the scheme. FIFA has committed to presenting a full report on the events to the FIFA Council, but the confederations criticized that commitment on the grounds that such a review would be conducted by FIFA itself, its staff, or by any stakeholder within football, rather than by a fully independent third party, per ESPN.

The three confederations have held preliminary discussions about organizing their own tournaments, ESPN reported, citing their stated goal of ensuring that players under their jurisdictions have meaningful opportunities to compete. UEFA has previously threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions, signaling the depth of organizational strain.

The confederations have stopped short of naming Infantino directly in calling for an independent review, but their statement makes clear they believe the process was fundamentally compromised. They are reportedly offering Infantino the chance to resign and leave his position with dignity without seeking re-election at the March leadership vote, according to ESPN.
